action: Block the device code flow in Entra Conditional Access (test in report-only mode first), review sign-ins using the Device code protocol, and tell staff to enter a device code only for sign-ins they started.
date_note: Date of Hornetsecurity's publication; the campaigns are described as seen in November 2026.
exec: Staff who approve a code on a real Microsoft page can give attackers a working Microsoft 365 session, even with MFA.
impact: No victim count or named victims are published.
plain: Fake payment emails lead people to a genuine Microsoft sign-in page and trick them into approving the attacker's login, giving access to their Microsoft 365 account.
summary: Hornetsecurity reported on November 19 several device-code phishing campaigns against Microsoft 365 users. Payment-notice emails carry ZIP files with HTML or SVG pages that lead to a fake SharePoint workspace and then to Microsoft's real device-authorisation page. If the victim enters the code, Microsoft issues tokens to the attacker's client. One loader was built from 475 obfuscated string fragments.
title: Hornetsecurity: device-code phishing with fake SharePoint payment documents targets Microsoft 365

validation.note: Hornetsecurity's own report (primary) and GBHackers' write-up both read; campaign scale and victims are not stated.
